# Feature parity matrix

Every Slack desktop feature from the three inventories (`docs/research/slack-features-{core,collab,shell}.md`, 1709 IDs) mapped to the private web-client APIs that implement it, with risk and build phase. API mappings come from the fact-checked `docs/research/api-*.md` references and their `verify-api-*.md` reports; GPUI constraints come from `docs/research/gpui-kit-guide.md`.

- **Rows:** one per feature; 153 overlapping IDs are folded into the row that covers them and listed in its Feature cell ("also: ..."), so the matrix has 1556 rows.
- **Risk:** `high` = private-API uncertainty (LEADS-only or FAILed verification), a missing GPUI component, or media/collaboration complexity; `med` = private/undocumented but observed API, or non-trivial custom UI; `low` = documented or well-observed API and stock UI.
- **Phase:** P3 Foundation crates, P4 Core UI, P5 Parity wave A, P6 Parity wave B. Features were moved off their default wave where the API research says so (e.g. clip recording and conversation tabs to P6, drafts/scheduled send to P4, user groups and channel posting permissions to P5).
- **"none (server-enforced)"** rows are plan/admin rules the server applies; the client only needs to surface the resulting errors or disabled states.
- **"not established"** rows have no API in the research; they are listed under [API coverage gaps](#api-coverage-gaps) and need live-traffic capture.
- Binding non-parity requirements (durable local history, etc.) live in [research/extra-features.md](research/extra-features.md) and are not rows here.

## Status summary

Re-audited on 2026-11-21 against the code as of that date (the app now runs live against Slack's web API with its own signed-in session): every planned, partial and deferred row was re-checked, statuses and evidence were updated where features have since been built, and the counts below were recomputed. Audited on 2026-11-19 against the code and verification docs from phases 1-5 (A+B): `docs/research/phase3-verification.md`, `phase4-verification.md`, `phase5-verification.md`, `phase5b-verification.md`, `phase6d-verification.md` (wave D: preferences, appearance, profile, status, DND, quick switcher), `phase6e-verification.md` (wave E: emoji picker and catalog, Block Kit and legacy attachments, shared message actions), `phase6f-verification.md` (wave F: slash commands, drafts & sent, scheduled send, workspace switching, keyboard shortcuts sheet), `phase6g-verification.md` (wave G: Later with reminders, pins and bookmarks, the Activity feed, dock badge and system notifications) and the screenshots in `docs/research/screenshots/`. Everything was checked in fixture mode, and nothing was exercised against a live workspace.

| Status    | Rows     | Meaning                                                                                 |
| --------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| done      | 135      | Built, with a screenshot, module or test as evidence                                    |
| partial   | 88       | Some of it is built; the Evidence cell says what is missing                             |
| planned   | 505      | Not started, and the API is known well enough to build it                               |
| deferred  | 828      | Cannot be built without a live Slack capture, a WebRTC media stack or the Quip protocol |
| **total** | **1556** |                                                                                         |

Top reasons for deferral:

1. **Undocumented API, live capture needed (785 rows).** These rows appear in [API coverage gaps](#api-coverage-gaps). The private call is either unobserved, known only from LEADS, or failed verification. Examples are Workflow Builder authoring, Slack AI and Slackbot, Agentforce, Slack Connect management, invitations, and huddle pre-flight, reaction and caption endpoints.
2. **Huddles need a WebRTC/Chime media stack (31 rows).** Native audio, video and screen share are huddle stages 2-4. They need the Chime protobuf signaling socket, DTLS-SRTP with relay-only ICE, and TURN refresh. Until then, only the join-in-browser fallback is possible.
3. **Live canvas and list editing needs the Quip collab protocol (12 rows).** Co-editing, comment anchors, text reactions and full-fidelity layout exist only in the undocumented Quip edit-document protocol.

What is built: the Foundation crates (`crates/slackless-*`: auth, API client, RTM, FTS5 store, core reducer, platform deep links, notifier and badge traits), and a dark-themed GPUI shell (`apps/slackless-gui`) with a workspace rail, sidebar sections, the conversation view with rich-text rendering, the composer, threads, reactions, message actions, DMs with presence, the channel browser, file and image cards, local FTS5 search, unread signals, and (wave D) a Preferences dialog with Light/Dark/System and colour themes, the profile pane, the status picker, the user menu with away/active and pause notifications, and the Cmd+K quick switcher. Wave E added the searchable emoji picker (categories, skin tones, frequently used, custom emoji), Block Kit rendering (section, divider, header, image, context, actions, input, with buttons, selects, overflow, date/time pickers, checkboxes, radios and text inputs) and legacy attachments, and one message-action set (hover bar and menu) shared by the transcript and threads; Block Kit interactions update local state only and send no `block_actions`. Wave F added the composer slash-command menu with 11 built-ins (/shrug, /away and /status run locally, the rest are logged), Drafts & sent (per-conversation drafts kept across conversation and workspace switches, plus Scheduled and Sent tabs), Schedule for later presets, switching between the two fixture workspaces (rail click, Cmd+1..9) with each workspace's state parked while away, and the Cmd+/ keyboard shortcuts sheet. Wave G added Later (saved messages with In progress / Archived / Completed tabs and "Remind me about this" reminders that fire system notifications), the pinned-messages panel and bookmarks bar, the Activity feed (mentions, reactions, thread replies with filters and read state), and the macOS dock badge (unread Activity + DMs) through `slackless-platform`. Wave D, E, F and G state is kept in memory in fixture mode; nothing is persisted or synced to Slack yet. There is also a headless CLI (`apps/slackless-cli`: search, read, send, reply, react, channels, dms, auth status). The CLI and the `skill/` folder are not parity rows. Since then the client has gone live (bridge.rs `CoreBridge::start`): channel details with editable topic and description, members and Slack Connect organizations, custom sidebar sections, the Join card and Leave channel, the Threads view and page, the image viewer with zoom and downloads, link and message unfurls, the directory (People and Channels), the search panel with recent searches and filters, the Activity feed on `activity.feed`, per-channel notification levels and mute, the macOS menu bar, the Huddles page with the browser fallback, and the New message view have all been built; see the rows for evidence.

## High-risk items

Grouped by shared risk. Each entry gives the concrete risk, the mitigation or staged plan from the research, and the affected rows.

### Huddles: native audio (Stage 2)

- **Risk:** Huddles are Amazon Chime SDK meetings over a private second WebSocket (protobuf JOIN/SUBSCRIBE), DTLS-SRTP with relay-only ICE, TURN credentials with a 300 s TTL whose refresh is unknown; webrtc-rs has a TURN-over-TCP gap and an SRTP AEAD-256 panic.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Follow api-huddles 'Effort estimate': Stage 0 presence/events (1-2 days), Stage 1 join-in-browser fallback (`https://app.slack.com/huddle/<team>/<room>`), Stage 2 native audio (3-6 weeks) on the slaq-proven stack (webrtc 0.12, prost, tokio-tungstenite, opus, cpal, sonora), AES128_CM_SHA1_80 first, encoded silence when muted, PING_PONG 10 s. Keep the browser fallback until Stage 2 passes a >5 min call (TURN refresh).
- **Rows (25):** F-COLLAB-001..002, F-COLLAB-006, F-COLLAB-010, F-COLLAB-032..034, F-COLLAB-039..045, F-COLLAB-047..051, F-COLLAB-053, F-COLLAB-059..060, F-COLLAB-074..076

### Huddles: video (Stage 3)

- **Risk:** Video send/receive needs INDEX/REMOTE_VIDEO_UPDATE handling, per-stream bitrate control, VP8/AV1 codecs and camera capture; background effects need segmentation that no crate in the research provides.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Stage 3 (2-4 weeks each for receive, then send) after audio ships; background blur/replace last or never (browser fallback).
- **Rows (5):** F-COLLAB-007, F-COLLAB-009, F-COLLAB-038, F-COLLAB-046, F-COLLAB-056

### Huddles: screen share (Stage 4)

- **Risk:** Screenshare is a separate `#content` attendee publishing video; receive needs RTP reassembly + AV1 decode (rav1d), send needs screen capture; the Chime screen-service URLs conflict with slaq's implementation.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Stage 4 (2-4 weeks): receive first, then send; reconcile `ScreenSharingUrl` vs `#content` attendee against a live capture before coding send.
- **Rows (4):** F-COLLAB-021..024

### Huddles: features with no observed protocol

- **Risk:** No endpoint or frame was observed for these huddle features (reactions/effects, hand raise, music, drawing, live captions, AI notes/transcription, scheduled huddles, external guests, `rooms.canJoinHuddle` FAILed verification).
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Leave them on the browser fallback; capture Chime DataMessages and Slack REST calls from a live huddle before scoping native work.
- **Rows (26):** F-COLLAB-025..031, F-COLLAB-035..037, F-COLLAB-054, F-COLLAB-057..058, F-COLLAB-061..069, F-COLLAB-071..073, F-SHELL-107

### Huddles: access pre-flight

- **Risk:** `rooms.canJoinHuddle` FAILed verification (source not reproducible) and access-request flows are unobserved.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Attempt `rooms.join` and surface its error; capture the pre-flight call before building a request-access UI.
- **Rows (1):** F-COLLAB-008

### Canvases: Quip-only editing and collaboration

- **Risk:** Full-fidelity canvas editing (co-editing, cover images, comment anchors, text reactions, callouts/layouts/dates) exists only through the undocumented Quip protobuf (`/canvas/collab/controller-init`, `load-data`, `fetch-latest`, `edit-document`), versioned per Quip build; markdown via `canvases.edit` cannot express them.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** api-canvases-lists staged plan: Stage 0 cards, Stage 1 read-only canvas from the HTML export (`url_private`) with live refetch, Stage 3 section edits through public `canvases.edit` behind a markdown round-trip fidelity gate, Stage 6 Quip protocol spike only after stages 1-5 ship. Everything Quip-only stays read-only or 'Open in Slack'.
- **Rows (12):** F-COLLAB-131, F-COLLAB-137..138, F-COLLAB-142, F-COLLAB-146, F-COLLAB-149, F-COLLAB-151, F-COLLAB-153, F-COLLAB-157, F-COLLAB-205..206, F-CORE-122

### Canvases: templates, AI and automations

- **Risk:** Canvas AI writing/editing, templates and canvas automations have no researched endpoints.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Render results read-only (they are ordinary canvas content); link out to Slack for authoring until a capture establishes the calls.
- **Rows (19):** F-COLLAB-175..181, F-COLLAB-188..193, F-COLLAB-207..212

### Lists: schema, views, history, automations

- **Risk:** List schema and view editing (`lists.columns.*`, `lists.views.*`), CSV import, version history and list automations are known by method name only.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Ship read-only Lists (Stage 2) and cell/item editing (Stage 4) first; capture schema/view calls before building field or saved-view editors.
- **Rows (27):** F-COLLAB-216, F-COLLAB-219..225, F-COLLAB-230, F-COLLAB-238, F-COLLAB-240..242, F-COLLAB-252..253, F-COLLAB-260, F-COLLAB-262..271, F-COLLAB-273

### Video/audio playback (files, clips, video blocks)

- **Risk:** No GPUI video/audio player; clip and video URLs (`mp4`/`hls`/`vtt` on files.slack.com) need the `d` cookie, so a stock HLS player cannot fetch them; `media_display_type`/transcription fields are only partly observed.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Stage it: poster frame + duration + open-in-browser first; then a native player (AVFoundation via objc2, or gstreamer/ffmpeg) behind a local cookie-injecting HTTP proxy; captions from `vtt`, resume via `media.progress.update`.
- **Rows (6):** F-COLLAB-111..112, F-COLLAB-114, F-COLLAB-733, F-CORE-126, F-CORE-129

### Clip recording

- **Risk:** Clip recording upload shape is unverified (`files.getUploadURL` with `subtype=slack_video`/`slack_audio`, container `mp4` vs `webm`), and capture needs camera/mic/screen pipelines GPUI does not provide.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Ship playback first (row group above). Record audio clips before video; capture one upload from the official client to pin `subtype`, `filetype` and `files.completeUpload` fields before building video capture.
- **Rows (12):** F-COLLAB-098..105, F-COLLAB-118, F-CORE-127..128, F-CORE-131

### Sign-in and credential acquisition

- **Risk:** Sign-in is entirely private API: the email flow is a CAPTCHA-gated `signup.checkEmail` -> `signin.confirmCode` -> `auth.loginMagic` chain, `d` is HttpOnly, and `xoxc` is no longer in served HTML (localStorage/LevelDB is the source of truth). Real `d`/`xoxc` lifetimes are unknown.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Ship the api-auth RECOMMENDATION order: (a) embedded webview sign-in reading `localConfig_v2` + `d` cookie, (c) import from an installed desktop app, (d) manual paste; recover a token from a live `d` via `app.slack.com/auth` or `ssb/redirect`; treat `invalid_auth`/`token_revoked` as a re-login prompt. Confirm wry exposes HttpOnly cookies before committing to (a).
- **Rows (1):** F-CORE-001

### Enterprise Grid

- **Risk:** Enterprise Grid splits methods between org-level and workspace tokens (`team_is_restricted`, `internal_error`), search needs the enterprise host and `frecency_ent_jumper`, and the `enterprise_id` websocket param was never observed.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Build per-workspace first; add Grid as a separate milestone validated against a live Grid org capture (token routing, `slack_route`, enterprise host). Until then show Grid workspaces as independent workspaces.
- **Rows (2):** F-CORE-007..008

### Dock/taskbar badges and menu-bar icon

- **Risk:** GPUI/gpui-kit has no dock-tile badge, no `NSStatusItem`, no taskbar/tray API (gpui-kit-guide section 14).
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Write a small `platform` crate with `objc2` (macOS `dockTile.badgeLabel`, `NSStatusItem`, `requestUserAttention`) and `windows`-rs equivalents, fed by the same unread model as the sidebar; ship macOS first.
- **Rows (4):** F-CORE-152..153, F-SHELL-168, F-SHELL-175

### Workflow Builder authoring

- **Risk:** Workflow Builder authoring (triggers, steps, branches, connectors, publishing, export/import, activity logs) has no researched API; only running workflows (`workflows.triggers.trip/info/list`) is covered.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Support discovering and running workflows natively; open Workflow Builder in the browser for authoring and management.
- **Rows (100):** F-COLLAB-314..318, F-COLLAB-320..322, F-COLLAB-324..325, F-COLLAB-327..331, F-COLLAB-333..335, F-COLLAB-337..345, F-COLLAB-347, F-COLLAB-349..357, F-COLLAB-359, F-COLLAB-361, F-COLLAB-363..366, F-COLLAB-368..369, F-COLLAB-371..373, F-COLLAB-375, F-COLLAB-377, F-COLLAB-380, F-COLLAB-389..403, F-COLLAB-405..408, F-COLLAB-410..415, F-COLLAB-418..420, F-COLLAB-423..424, F-COLLAB-430, F-COLLAB-433..434, F-COLLAB-436, F-COLLAB-439..441, F-COLLAB-443..449, F-COLLAB-451..454, F-COLLAB-462

### AI agents and assistant surfaces

- **Risk:** Agent/assistant surfaces (split view, streaming responses, agent sessions, code channels, Claude app, top-bar agents) have no researched endpoints or event shapes.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Render agent output that arrives as ordinary messages/Block Kit; capture the assistant-thread and streaming events from a live client before building dedicated agent UI; link out otherwise.
- **Rows (65):** F-COLLAB-497..499, F-COLLAB-501..511, F-COLLAB-513..519, F-COLLAB-565..577, F-COLLAB-580..584, F-COLLAB-587, F-COLLAB-589..590, F-COLLAB-634..640, F-COLLAB-693, F-COLLAB-695, F-COLLAB-697..710

### Slack AI, Slackbot and translation

- **Risk:** Slack AI / Slackbot / translation features (summaries, recaps, AI search answers, Today page, skills, tasks, translation) have no researched endpoints; they are plan-gated and server-driven.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Defer behind the rest of P6; capture traffic on an AI-enabled workspace first. Show AI content that arrives as messages/canvases; link out for the rest.
- **Rows (139):** F-COLLAB-896..902, F-COLLAB-904..937, F-COLLAB-943..944, F-COLLAB-946..950, F-COLLAB-953..963, F-COLLAB-967..978, F-COLLAB-980..1007, F-COLLAB-1009, F-COLLAB-1012..1013, F-COLLAB-1015..1045, F-COLLAB-1255..1259, F-COLLAB-1261

### Agentforce and Salesforce

- **Risk:** Agentforce and Salesforce surfaces (CRM sidebar, Sales Tracker, record pages) are app-driven and unresearched; some (sidebar, record editing) are custom first-party UI, not Block Kit.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Rely on the generic App Home / Block Kit / modal renderer; treat dedicated Salesforce UI as out of scope until a capture shows the calls.
- **Rows (91):** F-COLLAB-1051..1058, F-COLLAB-1061..1073, F-COLLAB-1075..1077, F-COLLAB-1079..1086, F-COLLAB-1088..1106, F-COLLAB-1108, F-COLLAB-1110..1111, F-COLLAB-1113..1121, F-COLLAB-1123..1126, F-COLLAB-1128..1130, F-COLLAB-1132..1135, F-COLLAB-1137..1142, F-COLLAB-1145..1150, F-COLLAB-1152..1156

### Work Objects

- **Risk:** Work Objects (entity unfurls, flexpane, edit-in-Slack) are a new unfurl surface with no researched client calls.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Fall back to the classic unfurl/attachment rendering and a link; capture the flexpane calls later.
- **Rows (10):** F-COLLAB-537..538, F-COLLAB-670..677

### Slack Connect directory and external DMs

- **Risk:** Slack Connect directory, external DM invitations, contact sharing and discoverability have no researched client endpoints beyond `conversations.inviteShared`/`acceptSharedInvite`/`listConnectInvites`.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Support accepting/declining invites and rendering external indicators natively; link out to Slack for directory and contact-sharing management.
- **Rows (25):** F-COLLAB-795, F-COLLAB-814, F-COLLAB-826, F-COLLAB-835..840, F-COLLAB-842..844, F-COLLAB-846..851, F-COLLAB-853, F-COLLAB-855, F-COLLAB-861..862, F-COLLAB-893..894, F-CORE-073

### Channel templates

- **Risk:** Channel templates compose canvases, lists and workflows server-side; no endpoint was researched.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Render channels created from templates normally (their tabs are canvases/lists/workflows); link out to create or customise templates.
- **Rows (32):** F-COLLAB-280..294, F-COLLAB-297..313

### Rich-text input in modals

- **Risk:** Rich-text input in modals/canvas needs a rich-text editor; gpui-kit offers a plain textarea and markdown/HTML display only.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Reuse the composer's rich-text model from P4; fall back to plain text input that submits a `rich_text` section.
- **Rows (2):** F-COLLAB-725, F-COLLAB-780

### Spellcheck

- **Risk:** Spellcheck needs native text-checking integration that GPUI's input does not expose.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Use macOS `NSSpellChecker` via objc2 against the composer text; ship after the composer is stable.
- **Rows (2):** F-SHELL-098..099

### Screen-reader support

- **Risk:** Screen-reader announcements and verbosity require platform accessibility APIs; the GPUI guide documents none.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Track upstream GPUI accessibility work; until then ensure keyboard navigation parity and expose plain-text message content.
- **Rows (4):** F-SHELL-105..106, F-SHELL-278..279

### Phone calls

- **Risk:** Outbound phone calls and incoming call declines go through calling apps or a Slack phone surface with no researched API.
- **Mitigation / staged plan:** Hand off to the calling app's URL / browser.
- **Rows (2):** F-COLLAB-081, F-COLLAB-090

## Phase plan

### P3

Foundation crates: auth, API client, realtime websocket, store/cache, rich-text model.

Directly user-visible rows: F-CORE-001, F-CORE-009. P3 otherwise delivers no rows on its own: it builds the crates every P4-P6 row depends on (session store and HTTP client with `token` + `d` cookie, websocket client with `hello`/`reconnect_url`/`tickle`/`presence_sub`, the local store that is the rendering source of truth per extra-features X-1, and the `rich_text`/mrkdwn model).

Implementers must read:

- [api-auth](research/api-auth.md): credential flows, required headers/cookies, `_x_*` params, session death
- [api-realtime](research/api-realtime.md): `client.userBoot`, `client.counts`, websocket connect/reconnect/resync, every event shape
- [api-messaging](research/api-messaging.md): message object, `rich_text` schema, `conversations.view/history/replies`
- [api-users](research/api-users.md): user/profile hydration (edge `users/info`), presence subscription
- [api-channels](research/api-channels.md): conversation list, sidebar sections model, `conversations.mark`
- [api-activity](research/api-activity.md): unread/badge model (`client.counts`, `*_marked`)
- [api-files](research/api-files.md): `url_private` cookie rules for the HTTP client
- [gpui-kit-guide](research/gpui-kit-guide.md): sections 1-2 and 13 (app init, entity model, async/tokio interop)
- [extra-features](research/extra-features.md): store and search requirements

### P4

Core UI: shell, sidebar, message list, composer, threads, reactions, message actions.

102 rows.

- **Core messaging: Workspaces & sign-in** - F-CORE-002..005
